neighbours.label: 'or'/'but' introducing an alternative possible outcome after a hedged clause
fire: The storm could weaken over the mountains, or it might grow even stronger.
Your package may arrive on time, or customs may hold it for a week.
The treatment might help your symptoms, or it could make them worse.
The bridge may hold for decades, but it could also fail without warning.
The talks could end in a deal tonight, or they may collapse entirely.
This drug lowers one risk, but it may also raise another.
The comet may break apart near the sun, or it could survive intact.
Prices might fall next spring, or they could keep climbing all year.
quiet: You can choose apples or oranges for the lunch box tomorrow.
Bring a pen or a pencil to the exam on Monday morning.
The shop sells red or blue jackets in every size.
We can meet on Tuesday or Wednesday after work.
Use salt or pepper to season the soup before serving.
The bus stops at the station or the library downtown.
Pick a book or a magazine from the shelf near the door.
Students may write in English or French on the test.

notes: card: ' or' x8, ' but', ' Or' after clauses with may/could; logit promotes would/should/might/may
